= Scoped declared and logical reference policies

SchemaNamePolicy keeps named_aliases_are_references enabled and logical_fixed_references_are_named disabled by default.
Existing global parsing and scoped policies retain their prior behavior.

A policy can exclude named aliases from resolving/parsed reference indexes while retaining RecordSchema, EnumSchema and FixedSchema alias metadata.
Declared names then remain independent when an alias matches another declaration, and an alias cannot resolve an in-progress recursive reference.
Field alias indexing remains controlled separately by record_field_lookup_uses_aliases.

A policy can preserve a named logical Decimal(Fixed) use as Schema::Ref instead of cloning the logical definition at every use.
The caller retains and resolves that name through the original logical-definition owner.
Schema::name and ordinary ResolvedSchema traversal do not discover Decimal's inner name automatically, so a consumer of this option supplies its known named logical schemas explicitly.
The original definition retains its physical Fixed name, properties and reader aliases.

Four additive regression functions cover default controls, parsed/resolving aliases, alias/declaration collisions and the owned logical-reference path.
They are source fixtures only under the Phase 1 work order; no compiler or regression execution has been performed.

A policy can parse a record field's actual type member independently with record_field_type_is_separate; the default is disabled.
Textual uses then pass through ordinary named-reference lookup even when the name is enum, fixed, array or map, and field-level logicalType does not change the child schema.
The surrounding field keeps its existing defaults, aliases, order and custom-attribute filtering; logicalType remains excluded from native field custom attributes.
Three additional source regressions cover nominal keyword names, flat versus nested logical metadata and a missing type member, with default-policy controls.

A policy can enable parse_references_in_input_order to consume and parse each reference before requesting the next.
On that route only preceding declarations and the current record's resolving name are available; later document bodies are never preloaded into input_schemas.
The default continues preloading all referenced documents and resolving forward dependencies.
The existing input_order vector retains duplicate-root checks and output order; a repeated root is rejected when encountered after earlier documents have parsed.
Each document starts with no inherited namespace, and the root parses after all referenced documents.
Three additional source regressions cover a small declared dependency sequence with nominal self recursion and default control, forward rejection, demand/iterator failure order, duplicate roots and namespace restoration.
